title: ChatGPT can transcribe as you speak now with Live Dictation
content:
ChatGPT can receive  audio prompts from your microphone faster now with a Live Dictation feature that transcribes as you speak, rather than waiting until you finish recording. It's rolling out now globally on all ChatGPT plans on the web, desktop app, and iOS and Android apps. While using dictation in ChatGPT, you can tap or click the audio waveform to show the live text transcript the AI is generating, then edit it in the prompt box when you're done.


Dictation in ChatGPT is getting faster and more reliable.

content:
Today is a new beginning for Anthropic: a years-in-the-making IPO that beat out SpaceX for most valuable of all time, having raised $81.3 billion and set an important precedent for the other public AI lab debuts to come. But it's not simply a financial milestone.

title: I let Apple’s always-listening AI summarize my life for two weeks
content:
Siri Recap can be turned on or off manually from the wrist.	

Was it worth it?
I've been asking myself this quite a bit over the last month or so while testing both the Amazon Bee Frontier and Siri Recap on the Apple Watch Ultra 4. Both enable a wearable to ambiently listen to your conversations and, using AI, summarize them for you. Why? So you can remember better and, hopefully, stay more present.
The main difference is that Amazon's Bee takes a maximalist (and frankly reality-bending) approach, whereas Apple is going for a more minimalist, privacy-first take. title: Canva adds an AI ‘off’ button
content:
Canva will now allow you to turn off its generative AI features. With this change, you can disable the graphic design platform's array of AI tools, such as its AI photo-extending Magic Expand feature, as well as turn off the ability to generate images with its Canva chatbot.
This toggle doesn't turn off every AI-powered feature on Canva, however. That includes Canva's background remover and its Magic Grab tool, which lets you select an object in an image and move it somewhere else. title: Tech lawsuits defined 2026 — and lawmakers want more
content:
With just a few weeks remaining, lawmakers are trying to pass new protections for victims of online harm before the end of 2026, targeting deepfake creators and online platforms that block users from filing lawsuits.
